section_summary: This section documents proposals, diplomatic consultations, and operational decisions concerning a SCAP-directed scientific fur seal investigation off Japan between November 1948 and June 1949. Originally proposed by the Natural Resources Section to collect up to 1,000 seals to study feeding habits and migration, the plan was scaled down to 200 animals following United States coordination with Canada and notification to the Soviet Union. In response to formal Soviet objections against any killing of seals prior to concluding a new multilateral convention, the United States directed SCAP to cancel the expedition, which was terminated in late March 1949 after taking 21 (or 22) seals. Subsequent records address shipping all collected specimens to the United States National Museum and Fish and Wildlife Service for scientific comparison with Pribilof herds prior to international division.

subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, US Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 730: Proposed Scientific Study of Fur Seals in Japanese Waters

subfiles.about: Announces a marine mammal research program and reports military commission sentences for the Palawan massacre.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, GHQ Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Announces Ford Wilkie's assignment under Dr. Oliver L. Austin Jr. to study seals, and reports Yokohama military commission sentences for the Palawan massacre.
subfiles.title: GHQ FEC Press Release No. 1630: Marine Mammal Study and Palawan Massacre Sentences

subfiles.about: Reports on NRS efforts and regulatory difficulties in securing authorization for a scientific fur seal expedition.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, US Political Adviser, Tokyo

subfiles.title: Airgram A-247: Proposed Scientific Expedition on Fur Seal Herds

subfiles.about: Transmits an approved NRS staff study and directive SCAPIN 1960 authorising two research vessels.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, US Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits an NRS staff study and SCAPIN 1960 authorizing two vessels for fur seal research, noting suspension pending consultation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 32: Scientific Study of Fur Seals to be Taken within Authorized Japanese Fishing Area

subfiles.about: Recommends directing the Japanese Government to operate two vessels to take fur seals for scientific research.
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, Lt. Col., Chief, Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Reviews sealing history and herd growth, recommending that two Japanese vessels collect up to 1,000 fur seals under SCAP supervision for research.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the Chief of Staff: Scientific Study of Fur Seals to be Taken within Authorized Japanese Fishing Area

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to provide two vessels for scientific fur seal collection.
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy, Colonel, Adjutant General, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Orders the Japanese Government to equip two 20-ton vessels at Muroran for SCAP-directed fur seal research through May 1949 under strict controls.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1960: Fur Seal Research in Japanese Coastal Waters

subfiles.about: Instructs the Embassy to notify the Soviet Government of SCAP's proposed fur seal investigation.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Instructs Embassy Moscow to deliver a note informing the Soviet Government of SCAP's planned fur seal study and requesting comments before February 20.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 40 to Moscow: Proposed Fur Seal Investigation

subfiles.about: Records a briefing given to a Canadian Embassy official regarding the proposed fur seal study.
subfiles.from: I. V. Davies, Office of the Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Records discussion with Mr. Wheelock of the Canadian Embassy explaining SCAP's fur seal research plan and historical sealing agreements.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Scientific Investigation of Fur Seals off the Coasts of Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits the text of the Moscow notification telegram for discreet discussion with Canadian officials.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Transmits telegram No. 40 to Moscow for Ottawa's information, permitting discussion with Canadian officials if they raise the subject.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 26 to Ottawa: Proposed Fur Seal Investigation

subfiles.about: Records an inquiry by Canadian official Wheelock regarding a Soviet response to the sealing proposal.
subfiles.from: I. V. Davies, Office of the Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Notes Mr. Wheelock's phone call inquiring about a Soviet reply and requesting that R. E. Collins be kept informed during his absence.
subfiles.title: Telephone Memorandum of Conversation: Proposed Fur Seals Investigation

subfiles.about: Authorizes SCAP to commence the fur seal expedition limited to 200 animals.
subfiles.from: Civil Affairs Division, Department of the Army (CSCAD / Maj. Cullen)
subfiles.summary: Authorizes immediate commencement of the expedition taking at most 200 seals for stomach analysis and directs division of pelts and skulls.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Classified Message WAR 85408: Approval of Fur Seal Expedition
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmits a draft cable for the Army to authorize SCAP's expedition with a 200-seal limit.
subfiles.from: W. E. S. Flory, Office of the Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Forwards a draft telegram for the Department of the Army approving SCAP's expedition for up to 200 seals for scientific stomach analysis.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Draft Telegram to SCAP: Fur Seal Investigation
subfiles.to: Robert A. Fearey, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Instructs Embassy Moscow to inform the Soviet Government that SCAP is proceeding with a 200-seal expedition.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Directs Embassy Moscow to notify the Soviet Government that in the absence of a reply, SCAP is proceeding with a 200-seal scientific expedition.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 146 to Moscow: Proceeding with Fur Seal Expedition

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of notes delivered to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding the fur seal study.
subfiles.from: Richard H. Davis, American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of Embassy notes No. 44 and No. 120 delivered to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning the sealing expedition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 149: Investigation of Fur Seals off Coast of Japan

subfiles.about: Informs the Soviet Government of SCAP's proposed fur seal study and requests comments.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Notifies the Soviet Government of SCAP's proposed scientific study of 500 to 1,000 fur seals and requests comments before February 20.
subfiles.title: Note No. 44 to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR

subfiles.about: Informs the Soviet Government that SCAP is commencing the expedition limited to 200 seals.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Advises the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs that SCAP is commencing the fur seal investigation immediately, limited to 200 animals.
subfiles.title: Note No. 120 to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR

subfiles.about: Reports Soviet Note No. 19 objecting to any SCAP examination of fur seals that requires killing animals.
subfiles.from: Foy D. Kohler, American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Reports receipt of Soviet Note No. 19 stating it is inexpedient for SCAP to conduct any seal examination requiring killing before a convention is concluded.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 664 from Moscow: Soviet Objection to Sealing Expedition

subfiles.about: Transmits telegrams regarding the sealing expedition and notes briefings provided to the Canadian Embassy.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Transmits telegrams sent to Moscow and records information provided to the Canadian Embassy regarding the expedition's reduction and cancellation.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 44 to Ottawa: Fur Seals of the Pacific Ocean

subfiles.about: Transmits copies and translations of Soviet Note No. 19 objecting to the fur seal expedition.
subfiles.from: Richard H. Davis, American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Transmits Russian text and English translation of Soviet Note No. 19 objecting to SCAP's sealing expedition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 155: Investigation of Fur Seals off Coast of Japan

subfiles.about: States Soviet opposition to any SCAP fur seal examination involving the killing of animals.
subfiles.from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR
subfiles.summary: Declares that pending negotiations for a permanent convention, the Soviet Government considers it inexpedient for SCAP to undertake any examination requiring seal killing.
subfiles.title: Note No. 19 from the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Russian Text and English Translation)

subfiles.about: Recommends immediate cancellation of SCAP's sealing expedition in light of Soviet opposition.
subfiles.from: Edward Castleman, Office of the Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Transmits a draft telegram advising SCAP that the US Government position is to cancel the sealing expedition immediately due to Soviet opposition.
subfiles.title: Memorandum and Draft Telegram to SCAP: Cancellation of Fur Seal Investigation
subfiles.to: Robert A. Fearey, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Transmits Embassy Note No. 230 informing the Soviet Government of the cancellation of the expedition.
subfiles.from: Richard H. Davis, American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of Embassy Note No. 230 delivered to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs reporting the expedition's termination.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 262: Correspondence with Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Informs the Soviet Government that SCAP cancelled the sealing expedition after taking 21 seals.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Informs the Soviet Government that in deference to its views, SCAP ordered operations halted on March 24 after taking 21 seals.
subfiles.title: Note No. 230 to the Soviet Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the USSR

subfiles.about: Reports the cessation of SCAP's sealing expedition on March 24 and the taking of 21 seals.
subfiles.from: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Informs Embassy Moscow that SCAP halted sealing operations on March 24 after taking 21 seals, with scientific data expected by August.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-96 to Moscow: Termination of Sealing Expedition

subfiles.about: Refers USPOLAD to WAR 85408 regarding the disposition of the pelts of the 22 seals taken.
subfiles.from: James E. Webb, Acting Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Directs USPOLAD Tokyo to WAR 85408 regarding the disposition of pelts from the 22 seals taken during SCAP operations.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-92 to Tokyo: Disposition of Pelts of Seals Taken

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese fishing area extensions, Antarctic whaling, and the cessation of fur sealing.
subfiles.from: Richard B. Finn, Office of the US Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reviews Japanese fishing area expansion, Antarctic whaling plans, and reports that NRS took 22 fur seals before ceasing operations per Washington instructions.
subfiles.title: Report on Japanese Fishing, Whaling, and Fur Sealing

subfiles.about: Records the loan of Moscow airgram A-461 to Alice Dunning.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Internal charge slip recording the loan of Moscow airgram A-461 to Dunning in the Division of Northeast Asian Affairs.
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip: Airgram A-461
subfiles.to: Alice Dunning, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.about: Reports delivery of Note No. 230 to the Soviet Foreign Ministry regarding the termination of sealing.
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Moscow
subfiles.summary: Reports transmitting Note No. 230 to the Soviet Foreign Ministry and explains omitting mention of scientific data transmission pending final decisions.

subfiles.about: Discusses Army reaction to the draft fur seal convention and Russian scientific catch provisions.
subfiles.from: Warren F. Looney, Office of the Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Records discussion with Army officials regarding preliminary approval of the draft fur seal convention and scientific catch limits under Article VI.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Proposed Fur Seal Convention

subfiles.about: Requests approval to send all 21 collected fur seal pelts and skulls to the Department of the Interior.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Requests permission to send all 21 seal pelts and skulls to the Department of the Interior for essential scientific comparison with Pribilof specimens.
subfiles.title: Telegram CX 50802 from SCAP: Request to Send Pelts and Skulls to Interior

subfiles.about: Recommends concurring with SCAP's request to send all 21 seal specimens to Interior.
subfiles.from: Wilbert M. Chapman, Special Assistant for Fisheries and Wildlife
subfiles.summary: Recommends transmitting an attached draft telegram concurring with SCAP's request to send all 21 seal pelts and skulls to Interior for study.

subfiles.to: Robert A. Fearey, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reports NRS plans to send all pelts and skulls to the US National Museum for comparison.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, US Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports that NRS intends to send all collected pelts and skulls to the US National Museum for comparison with Pribilof material prior to division.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-158: Disposition of Pelts and Skulls of Fur Seals
